reasons: The sys query selects otel_metric_type="gauge" and wraps it in rate(), but redis.cpu.time is a monotonic sum, and the dataset only holds sum types. The sys selector matches nothing, and rate() is applied to a gauge selector, which the rules forbid.
The user query correctly uses the monotonic sum with rate(); the sys query should use otel_metric_type="sum" with state="sys".

The $host template variable (prefix host, default *) is used in both Datadog queries but no host matcher appears in either PromQL, so the series set differs. It should become a matcher like host=~"$host" on the observed label (the dataset label name for host is not listed, so it needs checking).

avg without by-grouping matches the Datadog avg with no group-by, and the unit (s) and quantity (CPU time) are consistent with the definition; the Datadog redis.cpu.sys/user unit was not provided, so unit is only partially verifiable.
Outcome translated is appropriate since no functions or unsupported constructs are present.
